instructions:
Each item gives the geometry of a board, the rendered frame before an action, and the action. Predict the rendered frame after that action.

Cell codes are in `legend`. Walls never move. Exactly one player and exactly one box are on every board. The four actions are UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT.

Answer with the frame after, as a list of rows of integers, either bare or under the key `frame_after` -- so either [[0, 2], [4, 0]] or { "frame_after": [[0, 2], [4, 0]] } is accepted. Marking is whole-frame exact: a frame with one cell wrong scores the same as a frame with all of them wrong, because a theory that draws the world nearly right is a theory that has not been shown to draw it right.

If your theory has no rule covering an item, answer { "abstain": true }. That scores nothing, and it is recorded as an abstention rather than as a wrong answer; guessing costs you nothing here, so the distinction is for the reader of your report, not for your total.

The `tags` field says whether the transition occurred in the evidence you were given (`replay`) or did not (`heldout`). The two halves have the same mix of situations, so the tag tells you nothing about the answer.

world.description: A0: a self-built grid world with a figure and a movable object. Ground truth fully known, in neither pile. Its dynamics are what this paper asks about and are deliberately not stated here.
